notes: 4 sessions/week (upper/lower split with one full-body day rotation)
Rest 48–72 hours between sessions targeting the same muscle group.
Aim for 7–9 hours of sleep per night.
Add a drop set or rest-pause on the final set of isolation work in Weeks 7–8.
Week 12: reduce all sets by ~40% and keep RPE at 6.
Retest a 5-rep max on squat, bench, and deadlift (or a comparable benchmark) and log body weight and circumference measurements.

Track everything: Log load, reps, and RPE for each set. Review weekly.
Stall protocol: If a lift stalls for 2 consecutive weeks, reduce load by 5–10% and rebuild, or swap the variation.
Protein distribution: 4 meals of roughly 35–40 g protein, spaced 3–4 hours apart.
Post-training: Include 30–40 g protein within 2 hours of each session.

Prioritise carbs around training to fuel performance (roughly 3–5 g/kg/day for recreational lifters).
Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day.
Schedule one full rest day per week beyond the four training days.
Mobility: 5–10 minutes before each session, focusing on hips, thoracic spine, and shoulders.
Track body weight weekly (aim for +0.25–0.5 kg/week), session performance, sleep quality, and perceived fatigue. Reduce volume if performance drops for two consecutive sessions.
Week 4: Reassess working loads and technique; adjust starting weights for Phase 2.
Week 8: Body weight and measurements; check protein and calorie adherence.
Week 12: Retest benchmarks, measure body composition if available, and discuss next-block goals.

Before starting: Recommend a basic health screen and blood work (including ferritin, B12, vitamin D) with her GP, particularly given the vegan diet and the calorie surplus. Adjust the programme for any injuries or medical conditions.

raw_text:
# 12-Week Muscle Gain Programme

**Client profile:** 26-year-old female, strict vegan, recreational lifter, full gym access
**Goal:** Hypertrophy (muscle gain)
**Nutrition target:** 150 g protein/day from plant sources
**Training frequency:** 4 sessions/week (upper/lower split with one full-body day rotation)

---

## Programme Overview

| Phase | Weeks | Focus | Rep Range | Intensity (RPE) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 1: Foundation | 1–4 | Technique, work capacity, base volume | 10–15 | RPE 6–7 |
| Phase 2: Hypertrophy | 5–8 | Volume accumulation, progressive overload | 8–12 | RPE 7–8 |
| Phase 3: Intensification | 9–12 | Heavier loads, peak volume, deload in Week 12 | 6–10 | RPE 8–9 |

**Weekly structure:**
- Session A: Upper (horizontal emphasis)
- Session B: Lower (quad emphasis)
- Session C: Upper (vertical emphasis)
- Session D: Lower (posterior chain emphasis)

Rest 48–72 hours between sessions targeting the same muscle group. Aim for 7–9 hours of sleep per night.

---

## Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)

**Goal:** Establish movement quality, build a volume base, and learn progression logic. Use this phase to find working weights.

### Session A: Upper (Horizontal Emphasis)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dumbbell bench press | 3 × 10–12 | 90 s | 6–7 |
| Seated cable row | 3 × 10–12 | 90 s | 6–7 |
| Dumbbell shoulder press | 3 × 10–12 | 90 s | 6–7 |
| Lat pulldown | 3 × 10–12 | 90 s | 6–7 |
| Cable lateral raise | 3 × 12–15 | 60 s | 7 |
| Triceps pushdown | 2 × 12–15 | 60 s | 7 |
| Dumbbell curl | 2 × 12–15 | 60 s | 7 |

### Session B: Lower (Quad Emphasis)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Goblet squat | 3 × 10–12 | 90 s | 6–7 |
| Leg press | 3 × 12–15 | 90 s | 6–7 |
| Romanian deadlift (dumbbell) | 3 × 10–12 | 90 s | 6–7 |
| Leg extension | 2 × 12–15 | 60 s | 7 |
| Seated leg curl | 2 × 12–15 | 60 s | 7 |
| Standing calf raise | 3 × 12–15 | 60 s | 7 |
| Plank | 3 × 30–45 s | 45 s | — |

### Session C: Upper (Vertical Emphasis)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Incline dumbbell press | 3 × 10–12 | 90 s | 6–7 |
| Neutral-grip pull-up or assisted pull-up | 3 × 6–10 | 90 s | 6–7 |
| Arnold press | 3 × 10–12 | 90 s | 6–7 |
| Chest-supported row | 3 × 10–12 | 90 s | 6–7 |
| Face pull | 3 × 12–15 | 60 s | 7 |
| Overhead triceps extension | 2 × 12–15 | 60 s | 7 |
| Hammer curl | 2 × 12–15 | 60 s | 7 |

### Session D: Lower (Posterior Chain Emphasis)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Conventional deadlift or trap-bar deadlift | 3 × 6–8 | 2 min | 6–7 |
| Walking lunge | 3 × 10 per leg | 90 s | 6–7 |
| Hip thrust (barbell or machine) | 3 × 10–12 | 90 s | 6–7 |
| Lying leg curl | 3 × 12–15 | 60 s | 7 |
| Hip abduction machine | 2 × 15–20 | 60 s | 7 |
| Seated calf raise | 3 × 12–15 | 60 s | 7 |
| Dead bug | 3 × 8 per side | 45 s | — |

---

## Phase 2: Hypertrophy (Weeks 5–8)

**Goal:** Increase weekly volume and load. Add one set to the main compound lifts and push load up by roughly 2.5–5% each week where reps allow.

**Changes from Phase 1:**
- Main compounds: 4 sets instead of 3
- Rep range drops to 8–12
- RPE rises to 7–8
- Add a drop set or rest-pause on the final set of isolation work in Weeks 7–8

### Session A: Upper (Horizontal Emphasis)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dumbbell bench press | 4 × 8–10 | 2 min | 7–8 |
| Seated cable row | 4 × 8–10 | 2 min | 7–8 |
| Dumbbell shoulder press | 3 × 8–10 | 90 s | 7–8 |
| Lat pulldown | 3 × 8–10 | 90 s | 7–8 |
| Cable lateral raise | 3 × 12–15 | 60 s | 8 |
| Triceps pushdown | 3 × 10–12 | 60 s | 8 |
| Dumbbell curl | 3 × 10–12 | 60 s | 8 |

### Session B: Lower (Quad Emphasis)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Back squat or hack squat | 4 × 8–10 | 2–3 min | 7–8 |
| Leg press | 3 × 10–12 | 90 s | 7–8 |
| Romanian deadlift (barbell) | 3 × 8–10 | 2 min | 7–8 |
| Leg extension | 3 × 12–15 | 60 s | 8 |
| Seated leg curl | 3 × 12–15 | 60 s | 8 |
| Standing calf raise | 4 × 10–12 | 60 s | 8 |
| Ab wheel or cable crunch | 3 × 10–12 | 60 s | — |

### Session C: Upper (Vertical Emphasis)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Incline dumbbell press | 4 × 8–10 | 2 min | 7–8 |
| Weighted or assisted pull-up | 4 × 6–10 | 2 min | 7–8 |
| Arnold press | 3 × 8–10 | 90 s | 7–8 |
| Chest-supported row | 3 × 8–10 | 90 s | 7–8 |
| Face pull | 3 × 12–15 | 60 s | 8 |
| Overhead triceps extension | 3 × 10–12 | 60 s | 8 |
| Incline dumbbell curl | 3 × 10–12 | 60 s | 8 |

### Session D: Lower (Posterior Chain Emphasis)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trap-bar deadlift | 4 × 5–6 | 3 min | 7–8 |
| Bulgarian split squat | 3 × 8–10 per leg | 90 s | 7–8 |
| Barbell hip thrust | 4 × 8–10 | 2 min | 7–8 |
| Lying leg curl | 3 × 10–12 | 60 s | 8 |
| Hip abduction machine | 3 × 15–20 | 60 s | 8 |
| Seated calf raise | 3 × 12–15 | 60 s | 8 |
| Pallof press | 3 × 10 per side | 45 s | — |

---

## Phase 3: Intensification (Weeks 9–12)

**Goal:** Heavier loads on compounds, peak volume in Weeks 9–11, then a deload in Week 12 before retesting.

**Changes from Phase 2:**
- Compounds drop to 5–8 reps at RPE 8–9
- Isolation work stays at 10–15 reps
- Week 12: reduce all sets by ~40% and keep RPE at 6

### Session A: Upper (Horizontal Emphasis)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Barbell or dumbbell bench press | 4 × 6–8 | 2–3 min | 8–9 |
| Chest-supported row | 4 × 6–8 | 2 min | 8–9 |
| Dumbbell shoulder press | 3 × 6–8 | 2 min | 8–9 |
| Lat pulldown (close grip) | 3 × 8–10 | 90 s | 8–9 |
| Cable lateral raise | 4 × 12–15 | 60 s | 9 |
| Triceps pushdown (rope) | 3 × 10–12 | 60 s | 9 |
| Incline dumbbell curl | 3 × 10–12 | 60 s | 9 |

### Session B: Lower (Quad Emphasis)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Back squat | 4 × 6–8 | 3 min | 8–9 |
| Hack squat or leg press | 3 × 8–10 | 2 min | 8–9 |
| Romanian deadlift (barbell) | 3 × 6–8 | 2–3 min | 8–9 |
| Leg extension | 4 × 12–15 | 60 s | 9 |
| Seated leg curl | 3 × 10–12 | 60 s | 9 |
| Standing calf raise (paused) | 4 × 8–10 | 60 s | 9 |
| Hanging leg raise | 3 × 10–12 | 60 s | — |

### Session C: Upper (Vertical Emphasis)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Incline barbell press | 4 × 6–8 | 2–3 min | 8–9 |
| Weighted pull-up | 4 × 5–8 | 2–3 min | 8–9 |
| Seated Arnold press | 3 × 6–8 | 2 min | 8–9 |
| Single-arm dumbbell row | 3 × 8–10 per arm | 90 s | 8–9 |
| Face pull | 4 × 12–15 | 60 s | 9 |
| Skull crusher (EZ bar) | 3 × 10–12 | 60 s | 9 |
| Cable hammer curl | 3 × 10–12 | 60 s | 9 |

### Session D: Lower (Posterior Chain Emphasis)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest | RPE |
|---|---|---|---|
| Conventional deadlift | 4 × 4–6 | 3 min | 8–9 |
| Front squat or goblet squat (heavy) | 3 × 6–8 | 2–3 min | 8–9 |
| Barbell hip thrust | 4 × 6–8 | 2 min | 8–9 |
| Lying leg curl | 3 × 10–12 | 60 s | 9 |
| Hip abduction machine | 3 × 15–20 | 60 s | 9 |
| Seated calf raise | 4 × 10–12 | 60 s | 9 |
| Cable woodchop | 3 × 10 per side | 45 s | — |

### Week 12 Deload
Keep the same exercises but reduce sets by roughly 40% (e.g., 4 sets becomes 2–3), hold loads around 60–70% of Week 11 working weights, and keep RPE at about 6. Retest a 5-rep max on squat, bench, and deadlift (or a comparable benchmark) and log body weight and circumference measurements.

---

## Progression Rules

1. **Double progression:** When the client hits the top of the rep range on all working sets with good form, increase load by the smallest available increment (usually 1–2 kg for dumbbells, 2.5 kg for barbell).
2. **Track everything:** Log load, reps, and RPE for each set. Review weekly.
3. **Stall protocol:** If a lift stalls for 2 consecutive weeks, reduce load by 5–10% and rebuild, or swap the variation.

---

## Nutrition Plan (Plant-Based, 150 g Protein/Day)

### Protein Targets
- **Daily target:** 150 g protein (about 2.0 g/kg if she weighs ~75 kg; adjust to her actual body weight)
- **Distribution:** 4 meals of roughly 35–40 g protein, spaced 3–4 hours apart
- **Post-training:** Include 30–40 g protein within 2 hours of each session

### Key Plant Protein Sources
Plant proteins are often lower in leucine and sometimes lower in digestibility than animal proteins, so the strategy is to combine sources and eat slightly more total protein.

| Food | Protein per serving | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Seitan | ~25 g / 100 g | Highest protein density among whole foods |
| Tofu, firm | ~15–17 g / 100 g | Use extra-firm for stir-fries |
| Tempeh | ~19 g / 100 g | Fermented, good digestibility |
| Soy milk (fortified) | ~7 g / 250 ml | Good breakfast base |
| Pea protein powder | ~20–25 g / scoop | Choose a soy or pea-rice blend for complete amino acids |
| Lentils (cooked) | ~9 g / 100 g | Pair with rice for complete profile |
| Chickpeas (cooked) | ~8 g / 100 g | |
| Edamame | ~11 g / 100 g | |
| Hemp seeds | ~10 g / 30 g | Add to porridge or salads |
| Quinoa (cooked) | ~4 g / 100 g | Complete protein, modest amount |

### Sample Day (~150 g protein)
| Meal | Foods | Approx. protein |
|---|---|---|
| Breakfast | Soy-based overnight oats (400 ml fortified soy milk, 50 g oats, 2 tbsp hemp seeds, berries) | ~35 g |
| Lunch | Tofu and quinoa bowl (200 g extra-firm tofu, 150 g cooked quinoa, edamame, greens) | ~40 g |
| Pre/post-training snack | Pea-soy protein shake (1 scoop) with banana | ~25 g |
| Dinner | Lentil and tempeh chilli (100 g tempeh, 150 g cooked lentils, brown rice) | ~45 g |
| Evening | Soy yoghurt (vegan, high-protein) with nuts | ~15 g |
| **Total** | | **~160 g** |

### Practical Notes
- **Supplements:** Consider vitamin B12 (essential for vegans), vitamin D, and possibly omega-3 (algae-based DHA/EPA). Iron and zinc are worth checking via blood work, as plant sources are less bioavailable. Refer to a GP or dietitian for testing.
- **Calories:** For muscle gain, aim for a modest surplus of roughly 250–400 kcal/day above maintenance. Track intake for the first 2 weeks to calibrate.
- **Fibre:** High-protein plant diets are high in fibre. Increase gradually and ensure adequate fluid intake.
- **Carbohydrates:** Prioritise carbs around training to fuel performance (roughly 3–5 g/kg/day for recreational lifters).
- **Creatine monohydrate:** Evidence-supported and fully vegan-friendly (3–5 g/day). Worth discussing with the client.

---

## Recovery Guidelines

- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours nightly.
- **Stress and rest:** Schedule one full rest day per week beyond the four training days.
- **Mobility:** 5–10 minutes before each session, focusing on hips, thoracic spine, and shoulders.
- **Monitoring:** Track body weight weekly (aim for +0.25–0.5 kg/week), session performance, sleep quality, and perceived fatigue. Reduce volume if performance drops for two consecutive sessions.

---

## Checkpoints

- **Week 4:** Reassess working loads and technique; adjust starting weights for Phase 2.
- **Week 8:** Body weight and measurements; check protein and calorie adherence.
- **Week 12:** Retest benchmarks, measure body composition if available, and discuss next-block goals.

---

**Before starting:** Recommend a basic health screen and blood work (including ferritin, B12, vitamin D) with her GP, particularly given the vegan diet and the calorie surplus. Adjust the programme for any injuries or medical conditions.
